I’m a 78‑year‑old retired teacher who lives in the heart of Thủ Đức, Ho Chi Minh City, at 21.044412° N, 105.866207° E. After stepping down from the classroom 30 years ago, I’ve found that my daily routine revolves around keeping my body and mind active. Every morning, I lace up my sneakers and walk the short 0.28‑kilometre stretch to the city hall, a 7‑minute stroll that takes me past the bustling market stalls and the quiet park where I spot the local koi pond. I make that walk 11 to 13 times a week, mostly to run errands, visit friends at the community centre, and drop off a few parcels at the post office.

Walking is my preferred mode of transport because it saves me time and lets me enjoy the fresh air. I can dodge the traffic that often clogs the main roads and I’m able to arrive at my destinations with a pleasant, relaxed pace. Even though my household owns more than five motorcycles, I rarely use them—my joints simply can’t keep up. I do own four traditional bicycles, which I keep in the small storage under my balcony, but I reserve them for longer trips, like a weekend ride to the countryside or a visit to my sister in Ho Chi Minh’s district 2.

In retirement, I’ve taken up gardening on the balcony, tending to herbs and a few tomato plants, and I volunteer at the local seniors’ association, where we organize cultural evenings and craft workshops. I also enjoy reading biographies of Vietnamese historical figures and practicing simple Tai Chi in the park. My life is simple but full: a blend of gentle walks, community involvement, and the quiet satisfaction of a day well spent.
